messages:
anika: quick sync - did a tiny bring-up of a windowed speculative decoder with confidence-annealing on llama3-34b-q5_k. dropping notes here before we schedule the 100k holdout.

ciaran: windowed speculative? can you sketch the idea and high-level perf/quality?

anika: idea: only speculative-propose tokens inside a sliding window of N recent tokens (N=16) and apply a decaying confidence threshold per-token (anneal from 0.85 -> 0.65 over the first 6 tokens of any speculative streak). goal is to reduce runaway bias from long numeric sequences while keeping most short-token speedups.

rachel: neat. what were the quick numbers on latency / accuracy?

anika: canary (1.5k queries each) numbers below. baseline is our standard greedy q5_k.

```text
baseline greedy q5_k: median=48ms, p95=140ms, math_acc=79.2, truthqa=62.1
windowed-spec-anneal: median=20ms, p95=74ms, math_acc=78.3, truthqa=61.9
windowed-spec-no-anneal: median=19ms, p95=72ms, math_acc=77.6, truthqa=61.7
no-window-spec: median=17ms, p95=68ms, math_acc=76.8, truthqa=61.5
```

anika: notes: math drop is present but smaller with annealing than without (paired bootstrap p=0.04 vs baseline for no-anneal, p=0.13 with anneal). truthqa small drop not significant. Also saw less KV churn vs no-window approach (~+1% vs +7%).

sam: interesting that no-window was faster — expected since it speculates more. But tradeoffs look real. Any patterns in mistakes?

anika: yes: mistakes cluster on chained arithmetic where speculative tokens pick a plausible intermediate that later forces incorrect carry-overs. Anneal helps reduce that by tightening early acceptance. We also saw hallucination microbursts in creative-writing prompts when speculative_ratio high.

ciaran: what was the actual decode config?

anika: paste: 

```yaml
model: llama3-34b-q5_k
decode:
  mode: windowed-speculative
  window_size: 16
  speculative_ratio: 0.55
  anneal:
    enabled: true
    start_conf: 0.85
    end_conf: 0.65
    decay_tokens: 6
  beam_width: 2
  fallback_policy: conservative
kv_prefill: true
batch: 8
metrics: [latency, p95, math_acc, truthqa_em, kv_churn]
```

anika: fallback_policy routes to deterministic beam for the remainder of the sequence if a speculative abort happens. We also track per-request confidence curve to enable ROC-like thresholding later.

rachel: proposed holdouts?

anika: plan: 1) baseline, 2) annealed-window (this), 3) window-no-anneal, 4) no-window-spec, 5) annealed-window with speculative_ratio=0.4, 6) pattern-safety mode (regex detect digits/commas -> force deterministic decode). Each 100k queries stratified across slices: math MCQA, TruthfulQA, dialog 5k, summarization 2k. We'll run paired bootstrap and also compute per-slice token-hallucination rate.

ciaran: add a per-example trace log for 1k examples where spec triggered so we can inspect token-level transitions. Also record token entropy at trigger points.

anika: good call. I'll enable extended traces for the first 1k triggers per job.

sam: what's the rollback criteria if we roll to prod?

anika: canary at 1% traffic. Auto-rollback if math_acc drops >0.8 absolute (note: pretty strict) with p<0.01 after at least 10k queries, or if hallucination-rate increases >0.5% absolute. Also manual abort if KV churn >+10% on long sessions.

rachel: please tag infra for possible GPU throughput tuning; batch=8 numbers looked promising but we might need different batch sizing in Dedicated pools.

anika: ack - tagging @infra in the run doc. kicking off jobs now. ETA full holdouts ~4h. deploy-bot: deploy.request for job windowed-spec-anneal-holdout-6790012345 at 6790012355 by anika

deploy-bot: deploy.started for job windowed-spec-anneal-holdout-6790012345 at 6790012360
